'''Ilya Meyerovich Sobol'''' ({{langx|ru|Илья Меерович Соболь}}; 15 August 1926 – 9 December 2025) was a Russian mathematician, known for his work on [[Monte Carlo methods]]. His research spanned several applications, from nuclear studies to [[astrophysics]], and has contributed significantly to the field of [[sensitivity analysis]].

==Life and career==
Ilya Meyerovich Sobol' was born on 15 August 1926, in [[Panevėžys]], [[Lithuania]]. When [[World War II]] reached Lithuania, his family was evacuated to [[Izhevsk]]. Here Sobol' attended high school which he finished in 1943 with distinction. Sobol' then moved to Moscow at the Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics of [[Moscow State University]], where he graduated with distinction in 1948.<ref name="Kerimov">M. K. Kerimov, 2007, On the 80th Birthday of Il'ya Meyerovich Sobol', Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics, 47(7), 1065–1072.</ref> Ilya Meyerovich Sobol' recognized [[Aleksandr Khinchin]], [[Viktor Vladimirovich Nemytskii]], and [[A. Kolmogorov]] as his teachers.

In 1949, Sobol' joined a laboratory of the Geophysical Complex Expedition at the Institute of Geophysics of the USSR Academy of Sciences led by [[Andrey Nikolayevich Tikhonov]]. This laboratory was subsequently merged with the [[Keldysh Institute of Applied Mathematics|Institute of Applied Mathematics of the USSR Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=Kerimov />

Sobol' was for many years professor at the Department of Mathematical Physics of the [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]], and was an active contributor to  the ''Journal of Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics''.<ref name=Kerimov />

Sobol' died in Moscow on 9 December 2025, at the age of 99.<ref>{{Citation | vauthors=((Keldysh Institute)) | year=2025 | title=Obituary Prof. Sobol (in Russian) | url=https://keldysh.ru/sobol.pdf?ysclid=mj8dqceigi360530854}}</ref>

==Contribution ==
Sobol contributed to the scientific literature with about one hundred and seventy scientific papers and several textbooks.<ref name=Kerimov />

In his student years, Sobol' was actively engaged in solving various mathematical problems. His first scientific works concerning ordinary differential equations were published in renowned mathematical journals in 1948. Some of his subsequent studies were also devoted to this subject.<ref name=Kerimov /> During his years at the Institute of Applied Mathematics Sobol, he took part in the computations for the first Soviet atomic and hydrogen bombs. He also worked with [[Alexander Andreevich Samarskii|Alexander Samarskii]] on the computation of temperature waves.

In 1958, Sobol' started to work on [[pseudo-random number]]s, then to move on developing new approaches which were later called quasi-Monte Carlo methods (QMC).<ref name=Kerimov /> He was the first to use the Haar functions in mathematical applications. Sobol' defended his D.Sc. dissertation "The Method of Haar Series in the Theory of Quadrature Formulas" in 1972. The results were previously published in his well-known monograph "Multidimensional Quadrature Formulas and Haar Functions".<ref name="Sobol69">I.M. Sobol' Multidimensional Quadrature Formulas and Haar Functions, Nauka, Moscow, 1969 [in Russian].</ref>

Sobol' applied Monte Carlo methods in various scientific fields, including astrophysics. He was actively working with a prominent physicist [[Rashid Sunyaev]] on Monte-Carlo calculations of X-ray source spectra which led to discovery of the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, which is due to electrons associated with gas in galaxy clusters scattering the [[cosmic microwave background]] radiation.
<ref name="Sunyaev">L.A. Pozdniakov, I.M. Sobol', R.A. Sunyaev ''Comptonization and the shaping of X-ray source spectra - Monte-Carlo calculations'', Soviet Scientific Reviews, Section E: Astrophysics and Space Physics Reviews, 1983, 2, 189-331.</ref>

He was especially known for developing a new quasi-random number sequence known as LPτ sequence,<ref name="LPTAU1">I.M. Sobol', On the distribution of points in a cube and the approximate evaluation of integrals, USSR Comput. Maths. Math. Phys. 7 (1967) 86–112.</ref><ref name="LPTAU2">I.M. Sobol', Uniformly distributed sequences with an addition uniform property, USSR Comput. Maths. Math. Phys. 16 (1976) 236–242.</ref>
<ref name="Sobol2011">I. Sobol', D. Asotsky, A. Kreinin, S. Kucherenko. Construction and Comparison of High-Dimensional Sobol' Generators, 2011, Wilmott Journal, Nov, pp. 64-79</ref> or [[Sobol sequence|Sobol' sequence]]s. These are now known as digital (t,s)-sequences in base 2, and they can be used to construct digital (t,m,s)-nets. Sobol' demonstrated that these sequences are superior to many existing competing methods
(see a review in Bratley and Fox, 1988<ref name="Bratley">Bratley P., Fox B., "Sobol' quasirandom sequence generator", ACM Trans Math Software 1988; 14: 88–100.</ref> ). For this reason Sobol' sequences are widely used in many fields, including finance, for the evaluation of integrals,<ref name="Shuk">I.M. Sobol', B. V. Shukhman "Integration with Quasi-Random Sequences: Numerical Experience," Int. J. Modern Phys. 6 (2), 263–275 (1995).</ref> [[optimization]], [[experimental design]], [[sensitivity analysis]] and [http://www.broda.co.uk/software.html finance ].
<ref name="Jackel">P. Jackel, "Monte Carlo methods in finance", John Wiley & Sons, 2002.</ref><ref name="Glasserman">P. Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering Springer, 2003</ref> The key property of Sobol' sequences is that they provide greatly accelerated convergence rate in Monte Carlo integration when compared with what can be obtained using pseudo-random numbers. His achievements in astrophysics include application of Monte Carlo methods to the mathematical simulation of X-ray and gamma spectra of compact relativistic objects. He studied particle transmission (neutrons, photons). His contributions to [[sensitivity analysis]] include the development of the variance-based sensitivity indices which bear his name ([[Variance-based sensitivity analysis|Sobol' indices]]<ref name="Indices1">I.M. Sobol', Sensitivity analysis for non-linear mathematical models, Mathematical Modelling and Computational Experiment 1 (1993) 407–414; Translated from Russian: I.M. Sobol', Sensitivity estimates for nonlinear mathematical models, Matematicheskoe Modelirovanie 2 (1990) 112–118.</ref>
) and Derivative-based Global Sensitivity Measures ([[Derivative-based Global Sensitivity Measures|DGSM]]).<ref name="Indices2">I.M. Sobol', Global sensitivity indices for nonlinear mathematical models and their Monte Carlo estimates, Mathematics and Computers in Simulation 55 (2001) 271–280.
</ref><ref name="Indices1995a">I.M. Sobol', A. Saltelli, "Sensitivity Analysis of Nonlinear Mathematical Models: Numerical Experience," Mat. Model. 7 (11), 16–28, (1995).</ref><ref name="Indices1995b">I.M. Sobol', A. Saltelli, "About the Use of Rank Transformation in Sensitivity Analysis of Model Output," Reliability Eng. Syst. Safety 50 (3), 225–239 (1995). 
</ref> 
<ref name="Sobol2005">I. Sobol', S. Kucherenko, On global sensitivity analysis of quasi-Monte Carlo algorithms. Monte Carlo Methods and Simulation, 11, 1, 1-9, 2005</ref>
<ref name="Sobol2006">I. Sobol', S. Kucherenko, Global Sensitivity Indices for Nonlinear Mathematical Models. Review, Wilmott, 56-61, 1, 2005</ref>
<ref name="Sobol2009">I. Sobol', S. Kucherenko, Derivative based Global Sensitivity Measures and their link with global sensitivity indices, Mathematics and Computers in Simulation, V 79, Issue 10, pp. 3009-3017, June 2009</ref>

Sobol', together with R. Statnikov, proposed a new approach to the problems of [[multi-objective optimization]] and multi-objective decision making. This approach allows researchers and practitioners to solve the problems with non-differentiable objective functions and non-linear constraints. These results are described in their monograph.<ref name="Statnikov">I. M. Sobol', R.B. Statnikov, Selecting Optimal Parameters in Multicriteria Problems, 2nd Edition, Drofa, Moscow, 2006 (in Russian).</ref>
His book, ''Monte Carlo Methods'', originally published in Russian in 1968, had a US version in 1994.<ref name="BookMC">I.M. Sobol', A Primer for the Monte Carlo Method (CRC, USA, 1994).</ref> He also contributed to the first multi-author book on sensitivity analysis.<ref name="BookSA">Chan, K., Tarantola, S., Saltelli, A., and Ilya M. Sobol', 2000, Variance Based Methods, in Saltelli, A., Chan, K., Scott, M. Editors, 2000, Sensitivity Analysis, John Wiley & Sons publishers, Probability and Statistics series.</ref>

==Legacy==
Sobol's work is cited in textbooks of [[uncertainty quantification]],<ref name="R_Smith">{{cite book | vauthors=((Smith, R.)) | date=6 March 2014 | title=Uncertainty Quantification: Theory, Implementation, and Applications | publisher=SIAM | isbn=978-1-61197-321-1}}</ref> Financial Engineering,<ref>{{cite book | vauthors=((Glasserman, P.)) | date=7 August 2003 | title=Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering | publisher=Springer | edition=2003rd | isbn=978-0-387-00451-8}}</ref> quasi-Monte Carlo methods.<ref name="Lemieus">{{cite book | vauthors=((Lemieux, C.)) | date=27 February 2009 | title=Monte Carlo and Quasi-Monte Carlo Sampling | publisher=Springer | edition=2009th | isbn=978-0-387-78164-8}}</ref> His work on sensitivity analysis<ref name="Indices1"/> has been an inspiration for many different scholars.<ref name="Heredia">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Heredia, M. B.)), ((Prieur, C.)), ((Eckert, N.)) | journal=Reliability Engineering & System Safety | title=Nonparametric estimation of aggregated Sobol' indices: Application to a depth averaged snow avalanche model | volume=212 | article-number=107422 | date=1 August 2021 | issn=0951-8320 | doi=10.1016/j.ress.2020.107422}}</ref><ref name="Chastaing">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Chastaing, G.)), ((Gamboa, F.)), ((Prieur, C.)) | journal=Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation | title=Generalized Sobol sensitivity indices for dependent variables: numerical methods | volume=85 | issue=7 | pages=1306–1333 | publisher=Taylor & Francis | date=3 May 2015 | issn=0094-9655 | doi=10.1080/00949655.2014.960415| arxiv=1303.4372 }}</ref><ref name="Dimov">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Dimov, I.)), ((Georgieva, R.)) | journal=Mathematics and Computers in Simulation | title=Monte Carlo algorithms for evaluating Sobol' sensitivity indices | volume=81 | issue=3 | pages=506–514 | date=1 November 2010 | issn=0378-4754 | doi=10.1016/j.matcom.2009.09.005}}</ref>
